title: Indian Chickpea Curry
subtitle: with Roast Cauliflower and Bread Dippers
description: It’s plant power all the way with our super-tasty vegan dishes! Our meat-free, dairy-free, honey-free dishes are amped with plant-based proteins, fresh produce, nuts and seeds. Best of all, they’re for everyone, whether you’re vegan, vegetarian or flexitarian.

steps.text: Roast cauliflower: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line 2 oven trays with baking paper. Cut the cauliflower stem into 1cm chunks, then cut the head into small florets (see Make it faster). Put the cauliflower on a lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp vegetable oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast for 20-25 mins until golden and tender.

Start curry: Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander, keeping the leaves and stems separate. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Add the coriander stems, masala seasoning, half the tomato paste and half the garlic and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until fragrant.

Simmer curry: Add the chickpeas, tomatoes, coconut milk and 125ml (½ cup) water to the pan and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8 mins or until thickened. Stir in the roast cauliflower, half the coriander leaves and 1 tsp sugar. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Bake bread dippers: While the curry is cooking, cut 2 pita into triangles and put on the remaining lined tray. Drizzle with 1 tbs vegetable oil, scatter over the remaining garlic and toss to coat. Spread out in a single layer and season well with salt. Bake for 4-5 mins until golden and crisp.
Serve up: Divide the chickpea curry among bowls and scatter over the remaining coriander leaves. Serve with the bread dippers and enjoy!

Make it faster: Roasting cauliflower brings out its delicious nutty flavour. But if you'd like to speed things up, skip the roasting step and cook the cauliflower in the frypan for 5 mins or until browned before adding the aromatics in Step 2.
